the bell rule: down means 0.32 m (Castle Sound's number, its bricks are the same 0.30 m ones so its units are metres); a piece moved means 0.20 m (a brick width)
the bell is in reach of a big rod (an arc exists)
a big rod volley aimed at the bell drops it (Bell down after 1 rods)
the score counts shots, moved and standing, and they add up
replay: the same fort rebuilt and the same shots fed again give the same hash at the same step, and the bell falls again
replay keeps the event log (1 events)
Rebuild: the same fort comes back deterministically (hash equal over two rebuilds, and equal to the first build)
Rebuild resets the score (0 moved, bell up, no shots)
the same three rods give the same hash and the same moved count in two fresh sessions
fort replay code (250-piece castle, fixed volley) is repeatable: bcdf5115
perf run 250: exact count, settled, and a rod volley ran with at most 1 piece in 1000 put back by the tunnelling guard
perf run 1000: exact count, settled, and a rod volley ran with at most 1 piece in 1000 put back by the tunnelling guard

numbers.note: Node on a shared cloud CPU, one thread, software only, plain (no SIMD) Rapier. These are not iPad numbers and not any real device. The owner ran 4,000 pieces on an iPad and it ran fine; that is a report, not a measurement from this page.
